title: if and else
summary: `if (condition) { ... }` runs a block only when the condition is true. `else if` adds further choices and `else` catches everything left. Only the first branch that matches runs.
ideas:
1. Read a number and print "positive", "negative" or "zero".
2. Read three numbers and print the largest using only `if`.
3. Read a year and print whether it is a leap year.

cards.q: In an `if` / `else if` chain, how many branches can run?
cards.a:
At most one: the first whose condition is true

The chain stops at the first true condition. If none is true and there is no `else`, no branch runs at all.

The `;` ends the `if`, so the block always runs

`;` is an empty statement, so the `if` controls nothing. The braces after it are just an ordinary block that always runs.

A check at the start of a function that handles a bad case and returns immediately

A guard clause deals with the bad or unusual case first and returns, so the rest of the function can assume the normal case.

cards.q: Why does `else if (score >= 80)` not need to check `score < 90`?
cards.a:
It is only reached when the earlier test `score >= 90` was false

An `else if` only runs when every earlier condition was false, so `score < 90` is already known.
